newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Fighting in Somali capital kills five.
newsitem.headline: Fighting in Somali capital kills five.

text.p: Fighting in the Somali capital killed five people as a relative lull took hold among warring militias whose clashes have killed more than 100 people since December 13.
Witnesses said on Saturday that five people died and seven were wounded when two mortar rounds landed near the K-4 area of South Mogadishu on Friday night.
In New York both the U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali and the Security Council on Friday called on Somali factions to stop fighting and restore their ceasefire.

In separate but similar statements, the U.N. chief and the 15-member council said they supported all countries in the region attempting to negotiate a settlement in the civil war that shows little sign of abating.
Boutros-Ghali called "for an immediate cessation of hostilities and urges the Somali leaders to demonstrate political wisdom and patriotism".
The International Committee of the Red Cross said on Friday 1,500 people were admitted to Mogadishu hospitals between December 13-19 with wounds from the fighting.
It said 132 people had died of their wounds in hospitals but the overall death toll was probably much higher because people killed on the spot were not taken to hospitals.
The seaside Medina district is virtually besieged by forces loyal to south Mogadishu faction leader Hussein Aideed.

The fighting has pitted Aideed's militiamen against forces of his rivals -- Hassan Ali Osman Atto in south Mogadishu, Ali Mahdi Mohamed in north Mogadishu and Moslem fundamentalist leader Musa Sudi Yalahow in Medina.

Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine, succeeded his father Mohamed Farah Aideed on his death in August. He was elected president of Somalia by his supporters but both he and his government are rejected by most other faction leaders.
